title_en: Regulations on the Export Control of Dual-Use Items of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Export Control Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Export Control Law) and other laws for the purposes of safeguarding national security and interests, fulfilling international obligations such as non-proliferation, and strengthening and regulating the export control of dual-use items.

Article 2 These Regulations shall apply to the export control of dual-use items by the State.
Dual-use items as mentioned in these Regulations refer to goods, technologies, and services that have both civil and military uses or may contribute to enhancing military potential, in particular those that can be used for the design, development, production, or use of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery, including relevant technical data and other data.
Export control as mentioned in these Regulations refers to the adoption of prohibitive or restrictive measures by the State with respect to the transfer of dual-use items from within the territory of the People's Republic of China to outside the territory, and the provision of dual-use items by citizens, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations of the People's Republic of China to foreign organizations and individuals, including the commercial export of dual-use items and their transfer by means of donation, exhibition, cooperation, assistance, or other methods.

Article 3 The export control of dual-use items shall uphold the leadership of the Communist Party of China, adhere to a holistic approach to national security, maintain international peace, coordinate high-quality development and high-level security, improve the management and services for export control of dual-use items, and enhance the governance capacity for export control of dual-use items.
The export of dual-use items and related activities shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions, and shall not harm national security and interests.

Article 4 The national coordination mechanism for export control work shall be responsible for organizing and guiding the export control of dual-use items, and for coordinating major issues concerning the export control of dual-use items. The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall be responsible for the export control of dual-use items, and other relevant departments of the State shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the work related to the export control of dual-use items. The competent department of commerce under the State Council and other relevant departments of the State shall closely cooperate and strengthen information sharing.
The competent departments of commerce of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, upon entrustment by the competent department of commerce under the State Council, carry out work related to the export control of dual-use items.

Article 5 The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State, establish an expert consultation mechanism for export control of dual-use items to provide advisory opinions for the export control of dual-use items. Experts shall safeguard national security and interests, provide advisory opinions objectively, fairly, scientifically, and rigorously, and shall bear confidentiality obligations according to law for state secrets, work secrets, trade secrets, personal privacy, and personal information learned during consultations.

Article 6 The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall formulate and publish compliance guidelines for export control of dual-use items, to encourage and guide export operators and operators providing services such as freight forwarding, third-party e-commerce trading platforms, and financial services to export operators, to establish and improve internal compliance systems for export control of dual-use items, and to operate in a standardized manner according to law.

Article 7 The competent departments of commerce and foreign affairs under the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State, strengthen international cooperation on export control of dual-use items, and participate in the formulation of relevant international rules.
The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, in accordance with treaties or agreements concluded or acceded to, or on the principle of equality and mutual benefit, carry out cooperation and exchanges on export control of dual-use items with other countries, regions, and international organizations. Other relevant departments of the State shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, carry out cooperation and exchanges related to the export control of dual-use items.

Article 8 Relevant trade associations, chambers of commerce, and other industry self-regulatory organizations shall, in accordance with laws, regulations, and their articles of association, provide their members with services such as information consultation, publicity, and training related to the export control of dual-use items, and strengthen industry self-discipline.

Article 9 The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State, formulate and adjust the export control policies for dual-use items, and major policies among them shall be submitted to the State Council for approval, or to the State Council and the Central Military Commission for approval.

Article 11 The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations, based on the export control policies for dual-use items, and following the prescribed procedures, jointly with other relevant departments of the State, formulate and adjust the export control list of dual-use items, and publish it in a timely manner.
When formulating and adjusting the export control list of dual-use items, opinions may be solicited from relevant enterprises, chambers of commerce, trade associations, and other parties in an appropriate manner, and industrial investigations and assessments may be conducted when necessary.

Article 12 Based on the need to safeguard national security and interests and fulfill international obligations such as non-proliferation, upon approval by the State Council, or upon approval by the State Council and the Central Military Commission, the competent department of commerce under the State Council may impose temporary controls on goods, technologies, and services not included in the export control list of dual-use items, and shall make a public announcement. The duration of each temporary control shall not exceed two years. Before the expiration of a temporary control period, an assessment shall be conducted in a timely manner, and the following decisions shall be made based on the assessment results:
(1) if controls are no longer needed, the temporary controls shall be lifted;
(2) if controls need to continue but it is inappropriate to include the items in the export control list of dual-use items, the temporary controls shall be extended, but such extension shall not exceed two times; and
(3) if long-term controls are needed, the items shall be included in the export control list of dual-use items.

Article 13 Based on the need to safeguard national security and interests and fulfill international obligations such as non-proliferation, upon approval by the State Council, or upon approval by the State Council and the Central Military Commission, the competent department of commerce under the State Council may, jointly with other relevant departments of the State, prohibit the export of specific dual-use items, or prohibit the export of specific dual-use items to specific countries or regions of destination, specific organizations, and specific individuals.

Article 14 The State shall implement a licensing system for the export of dual-use items.
Where exporting dual-use items listed in the export control list of dual-use items or dual-use items subject to temporary control, the export operator shall apply to the competent department of commerce of the State Council for a license.
Where the relevant goods, technologies, or services fall under the circumstances specified in paragraph 3 of Article 12 of the Export Control Law, the export operator shall apply to the competent department of commerce of the State Council for a license in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations. Where laws, administrative regulations, or military regulations provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.
The export operator shall ascertain the performance indicators, main uses, etc. of the goods, technologies, and services to be exported, and determine whether they are dual-use items; if unable to determine, it may consult the competent department of commerce of the State Council, and the competent department of commerce of the State Council shall respond in a timely manner. Where the export operator provides consultation, it shall also provide the performance indicators, main uses of the goods, technologies, and services to be exported, and the reasons for being unable to determine whether they are dual-use items.

Article 15 Export of dual-use items shall be subject to obtaining a single license, a general license, or an export certificate through registration and information filing in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations.
A single license permits an export operator to conduct one export of a specific dual-use item to a single end-user within the scope, conditions, and validity period specified in the export license. The validity period of a single license shall not exceed one year. Where the export is completed within the validity period, the export license shall automatically cease to have effect.
A general license permits an export operator to conduct multiple exports of a specific dual-use item to one or more end-users within the scope, conditions, and validity period specified in the export license. The validity period of a general license shall not exceed three years.
Where an export is carried out by obtaining an export certificate through registration and information filing, the export operator shall complete registration with the competent department of commerce of the State Council before each export of a specific dual-use item, truthfully file the relevant information as prescribed, obtain the export certificate, and then export on its own by virtue of the export certificate.

Article 17 The competent department of commerce of the State Council shall, from the date of accepting an application for an export license for dual-use items, review the application either independently or jointly with relevant State departments in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations, and shall make a decision on whether to grant or deny the license within 45 working days. Where a license is granted, the competent department of commerce of the State Council shall issue an export license; where a license is denied, the applicant shall be notified in writing.
For the export of dual-use items that has a significant impact on national security and interests, the competent department of commerce of the State Council shall, jointly with relevant State departments, submit the matter to the State Council for approval, or to the State Council and the Central Military Commission for approval. Where approval by the State Council or by the State Council and the Central Military Commission is required, the time limit for review of the export license as provided in the preceding paragraph shall not apply.
Where, during the review of an export license application, the competent department of commerce of the State Council needs to arrange identification, seek expert opinions, or conduct on-site inspections of export operators or end-users in accordance with law, the time required for such activities shall not be counted within the time limit for review of the export license as provided in paragraph 1 of this Article.

Article 18 An export operator shall export dual-use items in accordance with the scope, conditions, and validity period specified in the export license and shall report the actual export transportation, arrival, installation, and use.
During the validity period of the export license, if the export operator needs to change key elements such as the type of dual-use items, the destination country or region, the end-user, or the end-use, it shall re-apply for an export license for dual-use items in accordance with these Regulations, return the original export license, and suspend the export temporarily.
During the validity period of the export license, if the export operator needs to change other non-key elements involved in the export of dual-use items, it shall submit an application to the competent department of commerce of the State Council for amendment of the export license for dual-use items, truthfully provide relevant supporting materials, and suspend the use of the export license temporarily. The competent department of commerce of the State Council shall, within 20 working days from the date of accepting the application for amendment, decide whether to grant the amendment and notify the export operator in writing. Where the amendment is granted, a new export license shall be issued and the original export license shall be canceled; where the amendment is not granted, the export operator shall export the dual-use items in accordance with the scope, conditions, and validity period specified in the original export license.
Where the competent department of commerce of the State Council discovers that the factors under Article 13 of the Export Control Law on which the approval of an export license for dual-use items was based have undergone significant changes, it shall notify the export operator to suspend the use of the export license temporarily. Upon verification, if the relevant changes may pose a significant risk to national security and interests or to the fulfillment of international obligations such as non-proliferation, it shall, in accordance with law, withdraw or revoke the relevant export license or require the export operator to apply for an amendment to the relevant export license for dual-use items; if there is no such risk, it shall promptly notify the export operator to resume the use of the relevant export license.

Article 21 The consignor or customs broker of export goods shall, when exporting dual-use items, present to the customs the export license issued by the competent department of commerce of the State Council and go through the customs declaration procedures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State; if unable to provide the export license, the customs shall not release the goods.

Article 22 Where the consignor of export goods fails to submit to or truthfully present to the customs the export license issued by the competent department of commerce of the State Council, and the customs has evidence indicating that the export goods may fall within the scope of export control of dual-use items, the customs shall raise a query to the consignor of export goods, and the consignor shall provide the customs with supporting materials such as the contract for the export goods, performance indicators, and main uses. During the period of the query, the customs may request the competent department of commerce of the State Council to organize identification and shall dispose of the matter in accordance with law based on the identification conclusion made by the competent department of commerce of the State Council. During the period of query and identification, the customs shall not release the export goods.
Where the export goods are subject to the circumstances specified in Article 14(3), Article 18(4), or Article 25 of these Regulations, and the competent department of commerce of the State Council becomes aware of the relevant circumstances, it shall promptly notify the customs; if, at the time the customs receives the notification from the competent department of commerce of the State Council, the export goods have been declared for export to the customs but have not yet been released, the customs shall not release them and shall dispose of them in accordance with law.

Article 23 The competent department of commerce of the State Council shall establish a risk management system for the end-users and end-uses of dual-use items, assess and verify the end-users and end-uses of dual-use items, and strengthen the management of end-users and end-uses.

Article 24 When applying for an export license for dual-use items, the export operator shall submit end-user and end-use certificates issued by the end-user. The competent department of commerce of the State Council may require the export operator to also submit end-user and end-use certificates issued or certified by the government authorities of the country or region where the end-user is located.
The end-user of dual-use items shall make a commitment as required by the competent department of commerce of the State Council, and shall not, without the permission of the competent department of commerce of the State Council, alter the end-use of the dual-use items or transfer them to any third party.

Article 26 The competent department of commerce of the State Council shall conduct verification of the end-users and end-uses of dual-use items in accordance with law, and the relevant organizations and individuals shall cooperate. Where an importer or end-user fails to cooperate with the verification or provide relevant supporting materials within the prescribed time limit, resulting in inability to verify the end-user or end-use of the dual-use items, the competent department of commerce of the State Council may include the relevant importer or end-user in a watch list.
An export operator that exports dual-use items to an importer or end-user included in the watch list may not apply for a general license or obtain an export certificate through registration and information filing; when applying for a single license, it shall submit a risk assessment report on the importer or end-user included in the watch list and make a commitment to comply with export control laws, regulations, and relevant requirements. The time limit for license review shall not be subject to the time limit specified in Article 17(1) of these Regulations.
Where the importer or end-user specified in paragraph 1 cooperates with the verification and it is verified that there is no unauthorized change of end-use or unauthorized transfer to a third party, the competent department of commerce of the State Council may remove it from the watch list.

Article 27 The export operator shall properly preserve the end-user and end-use certificates related to the export of dual-use items, as well as contracts, invoices, account books, documents, business correspondence, and other relevant materials, for a period of not less than five years. Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 30 Where an importer or end-user included in the control list cooperates with the investigation of the competent department of commerce of the State Council, truthfully states the relevant facts, ceases the illegal acts, proactively takes measures to eliminate the harmful consequences, makes and fulfills commitments as required, and no longer falls under the circumstances specified in Article 28 of these Regulations, it may apply to the competent department of commerce of the State Council for removal from the control list. The competent department of commerce of the State Council may, based on the actual circumstances, make a decision to remove it from the control list.

Article 31 The State shall establish and improve the enforcement cooperation system for export control of dual-use items, strengthen supervision over the entire process, and promptly detect, stop, and investigate illegal acts in the export of dual-use items.
The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, according to law, carry out supervision and enforcement of export activities of dual-use items.

Article 32 The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, alone or jointly with other relevant departments of the State, conduct supervision and inspection of export activities of dual-use items and investigate suspected illegal acts according to law. Relevant organizations and individuals shall cooperate and shall not refuse or obstruct.
The number of law enforcement personnel conducting supervision, inspection, and investigation shall not be fewer than two persons, and they shall proactively present their law enforcement credentials and relevant legal documents, and may take the measures prescribed in Article 28 of the Export Control Law; if there are fewer than two persons or if they fail to present their law enforcement credentials and relevant legal documents, the organizations and individuals under inspection or investigation have the right to refuse.

Article 33 The competent department of commerce under the State Council shall, ex officio or based on the need for organized identification raised by the customs, organize and carry out identification of relevant dual-use items, and may entrust relevant professional institutions or experts in relevant fields to provide identification opinions.

Article 34 Where the competent department of commerce under the State Council, ex officio or based on suggestions or reports from relevant parties, discovers that relevant organizations or individuals have risks of violating laws in the export of dual-use items, it may take measures such as regulatory talks and issuing warning letters.

Article 35 Where an export operator discovers or receives a notice from the competent department of commerce under the State Council that its export activities involve the circumstances specified in paragraph 3 of Article 14, paragraph 4 of Article 18, or Article 25 of these Regulations, it shall promptly report the relevant circumstances to the competent department of commerce under the State Council, take measures to eliminate or mitigate the harm as required, and cooperate with the investigation and handling.

Article 36 No organization or individual shall provide agency, freight forwarding, delivery, customs declaration, third-party e-commerce trading platform, or financial services for illegal acts in the export control of dual-use items. Where an operator providing agency, freight forwarding, delivery, customs declaration, third-party e-commerce trading platform, or financial services discovers suspected illegal acts in the export control of dual-use items, it shall promptly report to the competent department of commerce under the State Council, and the competent department of commerce under the State Council shall promptly verify and handle the matter.

Article 37 The competent department of commerce under the State Council may, based on applications from domestic import operators and end-users, issue end-user and end-use statements to the governments of other countries and regions, and carry out management of relevant matters.
Domestic import operators and end-users applying for end-user and end-use statements shall truthfully submit relevant materials as required by the competent department of commerce under the State Council, strictly fulfill the commitments made when obtaining the statements, and accept the supervision and inspection of the competent department of commerce under the State Council.

Article 38 Any citizen, legal person, or unincorporated organization of the People's Republic of China who receives a request from a foreign government for visits, on-site inspections, or the like related to export controls shall immediately report to the competent department of commerce of the State Council. Without the consent of the competent department of commerce of the State Council, no such citizen, legal person, or unincorporated organization may accept or agree to accept such visits, on-site inspections, or the like from a foreign government.

Article 40 Where an export operator violates the provisions of these Regulations by failing to perform the reporting obligation, it shall be given a warning and ordered to make corrections; if the circumstances are serious, its illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal turnover is 500,000 yuan or more, it shall also be fined not less than 5 times but not more than 10 times the illegal turnover; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 500,000 yuan, it shall also be fined not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 3 million yuan.
Where an operator providing services such as agency, freight, delivery, customs declaration, third-party e-commerce trading platforms, and finance violates Article 36 of these Regulations by failing to perform the reporting obligation, it shall be given a warning, ordered to make corrections, and may be fined not more than 100,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall also be fined not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 41 Any person who instigates or assists an export operator, importer, or end-user to circumvent the provisions of the Export Control Law and these Regulations and commit an illegal act shall be given a warning, ordered to cease the illegal act, and its illegal gains shall be confiscated; if the illegal gains are 100,000 yuan or more, it shall also be fined not less than 3 times but not more than 5 times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 100,000 yuan, it shall also be fined not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 42 Where a domestic import operator or end-user violates the commitments made to the competent department of commerce of the State Council, it shall be given a warning, ordered to make corrections, and its illegal gains shall be confiscated; if the illegal turnover is 500,000 yuan or more, it shall also be fined not less than 3 times but not more than 5 times the illegal turnover; if there is no illegal turnover or the illegal turnover is less than 500,000 yuan, it shall also be fined not less than 300,000 yuan but not more than 3 million yuan. The competent department of commerce of the State Council may, within five years from the date the penalty decision takes effect, refuse to accept its application for processing the statement on end-user and end-use.

Article 43 Any person who, in violation of these Regulations, accepts or agrees to accept a request from a foreign government for visits, on-site inspections, or the like related to export controls without authorization shall be given a warning and also be fined not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall also be fined not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 3 million yuan; if the circumstances are especially serious, it shall be ordered to suspend business for rectification.

Article 44 If an expert or professional institution providing consulting or identification opinions violates professional ethics and the provisions of these Regulations, it shall be given a notice of criticism and ordered to make corrections within a time limit; if the circumstances are serious, its qualification for consulting or identification shall be revoked, and corresponding legal liability shall be pursued according to law.

Article 45 The illegal acts of export control of dual-use items as specified in these Regulations shall be punished by the competent department of commerce of the State Council; if the law or administrative regulations provide that the customs shall impose punishment, the customs shall impose punishment in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations.

Article 46 Where any person violates the provisions of the Export Control Law and these Regulations, thereby endangering national security and interests, in addition to being punished in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations, it shall also be dealt with and punished in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, administrative regulations, and departmental rules.
If a violation of the Export Control Law and these Regulations constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 47 These Regulations shall apply to the export control of other goods, technologies, services, and other items related to the maintenance of national security and interests and the fulfillment of international obligations such as non-proliferation, as specified in Article 2 of the Export Control Law.
The export control of monitoring chemicals among dual-use items shall be governed by the provisions of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Monitoring Chemicals; matters not provided for in the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Monitoring Chemicals shall be handled by the competent department of industry and information technology of the State Council in accordance with the Export Control Law and these Regulations.
The export of items and technologies listed in Part I of the Missile and Related Items and Technologies Export Control List attached to the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Export Control of Missiles and Related Items and Technologies shall be included in the military products export management list and handled in accordance with the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Military Products Export and other relevant provisions.

Article 48 The transit, transshipment, through shipment, re-export of dual-use items, or export from special customs supervision areas and bonded supervision places to overseas, shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Export Control Law and these Regulations. Specific measures shall be formulated by the competent department of commerce of the State Council jointly with the General Administration of Customs.
Within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the movement of dual-use items between special customs supervision areas and bonded supervision places, or from outside such areas and places into them, shall not require export licenses and shall be supervised by the customs.

Article 49 Where an overseas organization or individual outside the territory of the People's Republic of China transfers or provides the following goods, technologies, or services to specific destination countries or regions, specific organizations or individuals, the competent department of commerce of the State Council may require relevant operators to handle the matter with reference to the relevant provisions of these Regulations:
(1) dual-use items manufactured outside the territory which contain, integrate, or are mixed with specific dual-use items originating in the People's Republic of China;
(2) dual-use items manufactured outside the territory using specific technologies or other dual-use items originating in the People's Republic of China; or
(3) specific dual-use items originating in the People's Republic of China.

Article 50 These Regulations shall come into force on December 1, 2024. The Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Export Control of Nuclear Dual-Use Items and Related Technologies, the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Export Control of Missiles and Related Items and Technologies, the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Export Control of Biological Dual-Use Items and Related Equipment and Technologies, and the Measures on the Export Control of Certain Chemicals and Related Equipment and Technologies shall be abolished simultaneously.
